title: Constraint-driven hybrid canary with counterfactual replay
author: Maya Patel
body:
Motivation: Many recent canary regressions are subtle and only visible when the candidate is exercised by real shadow traffic patterns. This PR introduces a constraint-driven hybrid canary flow that combines a phased traffic canary with sampled shadowing + counterfactual replay to produce low-latency, high-confidence roll decisions. The goal is to reduce false negatives in automated rollbacks while keeping rollout latency low and preserving cost budgets.

What this change does: Implements a new controller (HybridCanaryController) and a light-weight Counterfactual Replay subsystem that: 1) coordinates phased traffic increases by constraints (latency, p95 delta, request-level error delta, semantic-fidelity drift) instead of only fixed percentages; 2) samples shadow traffic for a bounded window and replays those requests offline against the candidate variant using the same request prefixes and cached KV state where applicable; 3) computes a replay scorecard and converts constraint violations into a single rollback_score that feeds into the existing RolloutEvaluator pipeline; 4) exposes new telemetry: replay_sample_rate, replay_latency_ms, replay_diff_rate, rollback_score, and constraint_breakers.

Key points and trade-offs: - Counterfactual replay is bounded: default sample is 1% of traffic for up to 10 minutes per step to limit cost and KV cache pressure. - The subsystem replays deterministically (same seed for sampling) to keep auditability. - Constraints are pluggable expressions (e.g., "p95(candidate) - p95(control) <= 40ms", "semantic_bleu(candidate,control) >= 0.92") and are evaluated per-step. - If the replay job detects a severe regression (rollback_score > 0.7) the canary aborts and triggers auto-backout hooks and a telemetry alert.

How to review (high level): - Focus on the controller lifecycle/state transitions (pkg/rollout/hybrid_canary_controller.go). - Verify counterfactual replay correctness and KV-cache substitution logic (pkg/replay/*). - Check telemetry contract additions (telemetry/metrics.yaml) and Grafana dashboard patch (dashboards/hybrid_canary_replay.json). - Confirm E2E scenario coverage in the new e2e/rollout_replay/ tests.

Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Replay engine + deterministic sampler - [x] Telemetry + dashboard updates - [x] Integration tests (local cluster) - [x] Docs: guide for hybrid canary + examples in quickstarts - [x] Security review for sampler/data handling

Testing and how to run: 1) Unit tests: run 'make test ./pkg/rollout ./pkg/replay' 2) Replay smoke: deploy the sample app in redwood/quickstarts/hybrid-canary and run 'scripts/run_replay_smoke.sh' (contains test vectors and a mocked KV store) 3) E2E: use 'make e2e-rollout' which runs the new scenario with synthetic traffic and compares rollback_score to golden threshold.

Rollout plan: - Stage 1: feature-flagged rollout in staging using 0.5% shadow sample and 5% initial canary weight. - Stage 2: increase sample to 1% and step canary to 20% after 10m if constraints pass. - Stage 3: full rollout to dedicated pools with replay off by default; on ramp per-customer via flag.

Observability and alerts: Adds replay-specific alerts: ReplayJobError, ReplayLatencyHigh (p95 > 300ms), ConstraintViolationSpike (>3 violations in 15m). Telemetry is exported to per-team dashboards and to the rollout-audit index for postmortem replays.

Backout and failure modes: - If replay subsystem OOMs or starts failing, the controller will automatically degrade to a conservative percentage-based canary (fallback mode) and emit an incident signal. - For partially completed replay windows we mark those steps "inconclusive" and require manual inspection before automated promotion.

Related: ENG-4821 (rollout policies), ENG-4893 (replay infra spike), SUP-712 (customer case where a canary passed metrics but broke a downstream transformer).

Commits summary: "Initial hybrid canary controller scaffolding"; "Deterministic replay sampler + engine"; "Telemetry and dashboard additions"; "E2E tests and quickstart example"; "Fix: handle KV cache misses during replay".

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps replay isolated from the main serving path (replay jobs run off-cluster worker pods) to minimize blast radius. The replay engine currently supports text generation and embedding evaluation vectors; extending to multimodal will be follow-up.

b2c3d4e - add deterministic sampling utility and sampling seeds
c3d4e5f - implement replay engine core + request normalization
d4e5f6a - telemetry metrics and dashboard JSON
f6a7b8c - fix: KV cache substitution edge cases during replay
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Left a request for clearer invariants around deterministic sampling and a unit test that seeds multiple runs to ensure identical sample sets. Also asked for a brief explanation of how stale KV entries are handled during replay.
Maya Patel: replied with details and pushed b2c3d4e; added deterministic sampler tests and update to docs explaining KV cache substitution with a bounded TTL and explicit mismatch counter.
Evan Liu: asked to limit default sample rate in staging to 0.1% to reduce cost; suggested a feature flag gate. I added feature flag support and updated the rollout plan in the PR body.
Priya Shah: ran local e2e and noted a flaky test 'ReplayJobTimeout' that failed intermittently; I added a retry/backoff and extended test timeouts in f6a7b8c. CI re-run passed.

Diego Ramos: approvals after the replay determinism tests and e2e fix.
Review summary: requested tests addressed, suggested follow-ups (multimodal replay, sample costing dashboard).
release_notes: Introduces a hybrid canary flow with counterfactual replay for higher-fidelity rollback decisions. Feature is behind a feature flag and opt-in per-environment. See docs/rollouts/hybrid_canary.md for usage.
merge_outcome_summary: After addressing deterministic sampling tests and an intermittent e2e timeout, CI passed and the PR was squash-merged. The replay subsystem is feature-flagged and will be enabled in staging for 0.5% sampling before broader rollout.

ENG-4893: follow-up to add multimodal request normalization
